column1: Pacific Crest Trail Water Report -- Northern California : Sierra City to Ashland, OR
Sierra City, CA to Ashland, OR
See Snow/Fords page for updates on Snow & Creek crossings & Road Closures in NorCal.

Never rely on water caches!!! Beware of contaminated water. Purify backcountry water.
FOR WATER CACHE TRAIL ANGELS : Water jugs, and caches, left unattended often end up as litter blown across the landscape. A little rope through the handles is a quick fix (if there is no other way to secure the bottles) but don't forget to revisit what you've left out! If you are going to put items out on trail please keep Leave No Trace principles in mind to preserve our trails.

All updates will remain on this report for 12 months. A representative sample of older updates will remain to provide context for water availability in previous years. You can send email updates to pctwater@gmail.com or phone/text (541) 728-3665 [voice mail/text only, no one will answer]. Waypoint IDs used in this water report are derived from Halfmile’s PCT maps which stopped receiving updates in 2019, as well as official PCTA IDs when available. Mileages were updated in 2025 using official PCTA mileage data.
Take fire safety seriously. Alcohol stoves start fires – go stoveless or carry a stove with a contained fuel source and a shut-off valve.

Water sources with blue text [marked with  * or **] have historically been more reliable. Sources marked with ** are more likely to have water year-round than those marked with a single *. Water described as seasonal, usually dry, early spring, etc. are less reliable.

column1: Note: The Sierra Buttes Reroute of the PCT (starting near mile 1204) was completed in the fall of 2017. This new trail is included in 2019 Halfmile Maps and the 2021 Halfmile Trail Notes and Guthook.This new section of trail replaced about 4.4 miles of old trail with 6.9 miles of new trail. The PCT is now 2.5 miles longer. The new section of trail takes PCT hikers and riders past lakes and camping. Plus, it avoids the old road walk and gets you further away from vehicle noises. The PCT passes the Packsaddle Campground at new trail mile 1208.4, which has a water pump behind the pit toilets.
